findings.title: The new `downsize` definition replaces the existing width/height API
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods by arity, so the definition at line 149 completely replaces the five-argument `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts = {})` defined immediately above it. Existing four-argument calls such as `downsize(input, output, 800, 600)` now bind `600` as `opts` and fail when `optimize` evaluates `opts[:allow_animation]`; existing five-argument calls fail with `ArgumentError`. Keep one compatible method signature (or use a differently named percentage-based helper) so existing resizing callers continue to work.

findings.title: ImageMagick is invoked on unbounded direct uploads before server-side validation
findings.body: The resize loop runs before `Upload.create_for` performs the normal upload validation at line 72, and there is no server-side maximum for the original multipart file before invoking `OptimizedImage.downsize`. The 10 MB check added in the JavaScript client can be bypassed with a direct request, so any logged-in user can submit a very large or highly compressed image declared by filename and make the application run ImageMagick up to five times before the upload is accepted or rejected. This creates an authenticated CPU/memory/disk denial-of-service path. Enforce a server-side source-file and image-dimension/resource limit before calling the converter.

findings.title: Client validation no longer honors the configured image and attachment limits
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` receives the upload type, but this change replaces both `max_image_size_kb` and `max_attachment_size_kb` with a fixed 10 MB limit. Sites configured to permit files larger than 10 MB are now blocked in the browser despite their settings, while attachments larger than a site's configured attachment limit are sent and only fail later on the server. The automatic-downsize allowance should be applied only to image source files while retaining the configured attachment limit and respecting configurations above 10 MB.

findings.title: Oversized animated GIF uploads are silently flattened when animated thumbnails are disabled
findings.body: The option passed here is `allow_animated_thumbnails`, but this operation rewrites the original uploaded file rather than a thumbnail. When that setting is false, `OptimizedImage.optimize` selects `downsize_instructions`, which invokes `convert` with `#{from}[0]` and therefore writes only the first GIF frame back to the upload tempfile. Users uploading an oversized animated GIF will receive a static GIF with no warning. Preserve all frames for original uploads, or reject/warn rather than silently replacing an animation with its first frame.
